stem: A health care facility identifies an adenovirus outbreak. Which additional outbreak-control measure may be included in the facility response?

options.A: Restrict visitors and new admissions when indicated as part of outbreak control
options.B: Stop hand hygiene because visitor restriction replaces standard infection-prevention practices
options.C: Allow symptomatic staff to continue working without assessment
options.D: Discontinue environmental cleaning until the outbreak has resolved

rationale: Current CDC adenovirus outbreak guidance states that appropriate infection-control measures in health care settings may include isolating ill patients, using PPE, restricting visitors and new admissions, monitoring staff for illness, environmental cleaning, and hand hygiene. Therefore A is correct. Visitor restriction is one possible outbreak measure rather than a replacement for other infection-prevention practices.
educational_objective: Recognize visitor and admission restrictions as possible components of a pathogen-specific health care outbreak response while continuing other infection-prevention measures.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_version_date: CDC page current as of 2025-2026; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Recommendations for potential outbreaks in healthcare settings: measures may include active surveillance, isolation/PPE, restricting visitors and new admissions, monitoring staff for illness, environmental cleaning, and hand hygiene
source_claim_supported: During a healthcare adenovirus outbreak, visitor and new-admission restrictions may be included among pathogen-specific infection-control measures.

correction_summary: Removed the overbroad claim that temporary visitor restrictions are a generic facility-wide requirement for any contagious respiratory outbreak. Reframed the item around current pathogen-specific CDC adenovirus outbreak guidance and retained conditional 'may be included' language.
audit_findings: A directly matches current CDC outbreak guidance. B, C and D contradict infection-prevention principles and the same CDC recommendation set. The item does not imply that visitor restrictions are mandatory in every outbreak or that they replace other precautions. No second answer or unresolved conflict remains.
